requirement: Each item's attachments appear in source order.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation: each item's attachments appear in source order.

`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[rust_attachments_keep_the_owner_kind_and_original_bytes]` is marked `{test}` for `requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.order`. It covers that obligation with a source that has several attachments on `fn f`:
- Two identical `/// café` doc comments.
- A `#[inline]` annotation.
- A trailing `// trailing` comment.

The test asserts the exact ordered list for that item: Comment, Comment, Annotation, trailing Comment. That order is source order. It also asserts that the first two attachments' spans don't overlap and are in order (`span.end <= span.start`). That check separates the two identical comments, which the content comparison alone can't.

The assertions would catch plausible violations:
- I read the implementation, `contents.rs#impl[Outline]#2/fn[from_legacy]`, to understand how attachments are built. It pushes all comments first and then all annotations, and then sorts by span start. If that sort were dropped, or if attachments were grouped by kind, the trailing comment would appear before `#[inline]`. The test's expected list would fail in that case.
- Reversing the two doc comments would fail the span-order assertion.
- The file-level attachment on item 0 and the empty list on item 1 also pass through the same path.

The test mixes the two attachment kinds and has a same-kind sequence. That is enough to cover the requirement. Other languages go through the same `from_legacy` path, so the obligation has no further distinct modes or boundary cases to test.

text: Each item's attachments appear in source order.
